 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating temporal dynamics from multiple concurrent interests. [MiaSRec (SIGIR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00986) explicitly challenges last-item dominance: it constructs item-centered session representations and dynamically selects important intents, reporting stronger gains on longer sessions. [MTMISRec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417425008887) partitions histories using an interaction-gap threshold and models within-session and between-session dependencies; its segmentation is threshold-based rather than learned, and its attribute integration requires checking feature availability. [SS4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08132) combines time-aware and relation-aware state-space models, with discretization steps controlled by observed time intervals and input content. [TiM4Rec (2024 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16182) introduces a time-aware structured mask into a Mamba2-style architecture, targeting efficient temporal modeling at low embedding dimensions.

Research implication, rather than an established result: test a small causal bank of interest states with soft routing from item embeddings and log time gaps, plus a learned boundary/reset gate. Retain a last-item residual and compare against SASRec, last-item-only, one-state recurrence, fixed-window pooling, and fixed-gap segmentation under matched capacity. These sources motivate the components but do not establish improvement on the four specified Amazon categories or pinned HR@10 protocol. To separate recency from positional effects, preserve sequence length and positions while masking item content; separately ablate or shuffle historical gaps while preserving item order. Use only timestamps already observed at each prediction prefix. Select using macro validation HR@10 and inspect routing collapse, state utilization, and sensitivity to history length.

---

Recent work supports finer matching, but several close matches violate the no-pretrained-model constraint. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware user/item representations and scores attribute-wise interactions, offering an architectural precedent for preserving distinct interests rather than compressing everything into one vector; its text pipeline uses pretrained language models. [FineRec (SIGIR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12975) builds attribute-specific graphs from review attribute–opinion pairs extracted by an LLM, making its pipeline unsuitable when reviews and pretrained models are unavailable. [C-TLSAN (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13021) integrates product-description content into long- and short-term attention, supporting content–temporal fusion, though its abstract does not establish a text encoder trained from scratch.

The clearest candidate-conditioned precedent found is older: [Multi-Level Interaction Reranking (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09370) explicitly models candidate–history and feature-level interactions with personalized long-/short-term attention. Practical adaptation, proposed here rather than established by these papers: retain SASRec and add candidate-query attention over historical collaborative embeddings, plus a separate title/description matching branch using TF-IDF or trainable token embeddings. Combine maximum, recency-weighted and attention-pooled similarities through a small gated scoring head; ablate collaborative-only, text-only and combined variants using the fixed macro validation HR@10. This search did not establish a directly matching 2024–2026 method combining candidate-conditioned history matching with scratch-trained text. Metadata overlap supplies relevance evidence, but cannot establish ownership, compatibility or satisfied demand.

Objective-only evidence supports testing multiple negatives before changing SASRec’s architecture. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract; original RecSys 2023)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) combines increased negative counts with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence. This addresses calibration and training stability, not false-negative identification. [A Theoretical Analysis of Recommendation Loss Functions under Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11228603) finds categorical cross-entropy and BPR equivalent with one negative; conclusions favoring full-catalog cross-entropy do not automatically transfer to sampled training. Compare multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and sampled softmax under matched compute.

For adaptive hardness, [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) uses uniform-negative warm-up, efficient approximate global recall, and curriculum re-ranking. It reports that introducing hard negatives too early can underperform uniform sampling. Random selection among several high-scoring candidates mitigates false-negative risk; highest score alone does not establish a true negative. A cheaper experimental adaptation would warm up uniformly, then gradually mix uniform negatives with randomly selected top-ranked candidates from a modest pool, excluding observed training interactions. This adaptation remains a hypothesis for the benchmark.
